# Risk model validation (generated by concierge/risk.py)

Reference storm: 2025-02-12..2025-02-18 (**Observed** damage records). Model: Poisson regression of line-damage records (primary, secondary, pole) per circuit with overhead miles as exposure, L2 alpha = 0.05, 108 circuits with overhead line.

## Coefficients (per 1 standard deviation of the feature; log-rate scale)

| feature | coefficient | mean | sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| oh_share | -0.192 | 0.749 | 0.188 |
| lateral_share | -0.232 | 0.663 | 0.218 |
| pole_year_centered | -0.055 | -0.001 | 0.900 |
| pole_year_known | -0.367 | 0.429 | 0.209 |
| intercept | -0.693 | | |

Territory line-damage rate: 0.468 per overhead mile (median circuit 0.085). Equipment rate: 0.0134 per unit (366 records / 27383 units). Service-line rate: 0.00140 per overhead customer (91 records / 64824 customers).

## Zone-level shrinkage (empirical Bayes)

The circuit model is the prior mean μ for each zone; the zone's own Feb-2025 count n moves it to the gamma-Poisson posterior λ = μ·(α+n)/(α+μ). Negative-binomial MLE over 7,190 zones gives α_line = 0.119 and α_equipment = 0.172 (small α = damage was highly concentrated, so observed counts dominate where they exist).

Zones with Feb-2025 line damage: 373; sum of posterior λ_line = 919 vs observed 881 and prior 881.

## Leave-one-circuit-out validation of the prior (circuit model)

| metric | model | exposure-only baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Spearman rank correlation (predicted vs observed counts) | 0.658 | 0.644 |
| Mean absolute error (records per circuit) | 8.83 | 8.63 |

Calibration by predicted quintile (sums of records):

| quintile | circuits | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 22 | 33.2 | 4 |
| 2 | 22 | 73.4 | 43 |
| 3 | 22 | 104.2 | 76 |
| 4 | 21 | 160.1 | 103 |
| 5 | 21 | 442.6 | 655 |

## Customer risk distribution at severity 1x (Feb-2025-like storm)

| band | customers |
|---|---|
| Low | 496 |
| Moderate | 60,113 |
| High | 27,756 |
| Very high | 29,230 |

Median customer hazard Λ = 0.498 → P = 39.2%; 90th percentile P = 91.5%.
Customers on the 45 circuits with no Feb-2025 damage: median P = 30.1%; on circuits with damage: median P = 43.5%.

Observed anchor: in Feb-2025, damage sat on the upstream path of 29.4% of pathed customers territory-wide (per-circuit share ranges 0%–100%).

## Limitations

- One reference storm: the model learns *where* damage concentrated in that event, not how any future storm will behave; where the storm hit and how vulnerable the lines are cannot be separated with one event.
- The storm footprint is assumed to have covered every circuit in the extract (zero-damage circuits count as zeros).
- No per-customer outage records exist; the probability is a damage-intensity estimate, not a calibrated outage forecast.
- Tie switches / back-feeds are not modelled; any damage on the upstream path is assumed to interrupt service.
